_superseded_note: This 3-arm (baseline/intact/degraded) shape is superseded by two separate 2-arm declarations - pilot-discrimination-declaration.json (intact vs degraded, skillc.calibration's new discrimination-declaration kind) and pilot-improvement-declaration.json (intact vs baseline, an ordinary calibration-declaration) - per orchestrator review comment 6025311708. parse_declaration cannot express this 3-arm shape at all: its two treated arms must share an identical subject, and a degraded arm's revision never matches intact's (confirmed directly, not assumed). The cost cap this file's 'design' section cites is also superseded (operator ruling, comment 6021089903: cost is not a constraint). Kept as the historical record of #287's first preparation pass; see README.md's own superseded banner.
_comment: Preparation draft for skillc #287 (#288's prerequisite). Every value marked PENDING below is an explicit placeholder, not a guess: this file does not parse under skillc.calibration.parse_declaration and is not meant to yet - attempts_per_arm, the arms' subjects and shared.model/client are all open questions this file names rather than invents answers for. See README.md for what each PENDING depends on, the two discriminating-case risks (#150's non-discriminating result; calibration.py's MAX_ATTEMPTS_PER_ARM=8 cap against power_cost_table.json's n>=10 rows), and power_cost_table.py/.json for the computed sizing this declaration must cite once #270/#271 land. No live run is authorized by this file (ADR 0005); 'approval' stays null until the operator rules on pilot-spend authorization separately from filing or drafting this.

design.secondary_contrast: intact CPP subject vs baseline (no subject installed) - the improvement question #288's outcome contract (#245) asks for, sharing the intact arm's attempts with the discrimination contrast above rather than running a fourth arm.

attempts_per_arm: PENDING #270/#271 pilot - see power_cost_table.json's rows for n in {10, 15, 20, 30} and README 'Design risk 2': skillc.calibration.MAX_ATTEMPTS_PER_ARM is 8 today, below every n this table computes as plausibly necessary; the declaration cannot name a final attempts_per_arm until either the pilot shows a strong enough effect size to fit within 3-8, or that cap is revisited (Nit Store finding, not fixed by this preparation issue)

tolerance.test: one-sided Fisher's exact, two instances: (1) discrimination - intact vs degraded; (2) improvement - intact vs baseline
tolerance.non_evaluable_outcome: PENDING #270/#271 + pilot: what counts as a non-evaluable attempt for THIS case (timeout, crash, grader UNKNOWN) and whether it is excluded from the Fisher table or counted against its own arm - #288 acceptance item 2 ('retain... unknown coverage') requires this be fixed in advance, not decided post hoc from whichever attempts happen to come back unevaluable

design_risks.statement: The only live discriminating-run attempt to date (finish-close-ref, NORMAL vs DEGRADED, both PASS) was NON-DISCRIMINATING; cause unresolved between (a) the model's default behaviour needing no CPP instruction, and (b) residual CPP content still present in the degraded arm (e.g. gh-pr-merge.sh's own negation-handling code) despite the prose rule's removal. #287's declaration must name, for its OWN case, precisely what the degraded arm removes and verify via `skillc profile diagnose` (#295) that no other installed skill or helper still carries equivalent content - a repeat of #150's shape (removing the stated rule while something else still enforces it) would reproduce a non-discriminating result at whatever n is chosen, wasting the whole run regardless of power.

power_cost_table.py's computed rows show that even at the most favorable observable outcome (the intact arm passing every attempt), the degraded arm must fail roughly 40%+ of its attempts at n=10 (or ~17%+ at n=30) for a one-sided Fisher's exact test to reach p<0.05. calibration.py's own schema refuses attempts_per_arm outside 3-8 (skillc/calibration.py:324-325), which this table never reaches at n=10. Either the eventual pilot shows an effect size strong enough to fit within 3-8 attempts per arm, or #287/#288 cannot run through calibration.py's existing parse_declaration/runner unmodified. This preparation issue does not resolve it (recorded on skillc's Nit Store issue #20, not fixed here).
